science-source-y8-safety-bay-2024-matter.title: Year 8 Science — Matter — Safety Bay 2024 (original assessment)
science-source-y8-safety-bay-2024-matter.coverage: Exact original assessment. All written and diagram questions remain in the question bank, builder and practice; only valid MC enter battles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a physical property of substances?
options: the temperature at which a substance will boil
how a substance reacts when combined with another substance
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — D. how a substance reacts when combined with another substance. Chemical properties describe behaviour in chemical reactions; the other options are physical properties.

options: all matter is made of atoms that have no mass and are too small to be seen with the naked eye.
some matter is made of atoms that have mass and are small, but can be seen with the naked eye.
all matter is made of atoms that have mass and are small, but can be seen with the naked eye.
all matter is made of atoms that have mass but are too small to be seen with the naked eye.
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — D. all matter is made of atoms that have mass but are too small to be seen with the naked eye.. D is the intended school-model answer. Particles have mass and individual atoms are too small to see unaided. Matter may contain atoms, molecules or ions.

questions.prompt: Melting point is the temperature at which a
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — D. solid changes to a liquid.. Melting is the change from solid to liquid.

questions.prompt: Describe the particles in a solid. The particles in a solid are
options: strongly attracted to each other so the solid has a definite shape.
strongly attracted to each other so the solid does not have a definite shape.
weakly attracted to each other so the solid has a definite shape.
weakly attracted to each other so the solid does not have a definite shape.
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — A. strongly attracted to each other so the solid has a definite shape.. Strong attractions hold particles around fixed positions, giving a solid a definite shape.

questions.prompt: Elements are represented by chemical symbol.  Symbols are written with:
options: at least and ONLY one capital letter
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — D. at least and ONLY one capital letter. A chemical symbol starts with one capital letter; any following letters are lower-case. The answer document has a different Question 6 about attractions between particles.

questions.prompt: What is usually required for a change in the state of matter of a substance? A change in the
options: chemical potential energy of the atoms.
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — D. amount of heat energy.. D is intended: thermal energy is usually transferred during a change of state; the atoms do not change identity.

questions.prompt: As a solid object is heated, its particles:
options: vibrate less rapidly and cause it to contract.
vibrate more rapidly and cause it to expand.
attract each other more, causing contraction.
shrink in size so the gaps between them increase.
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — B. vibrate more rapidly and cause it to expand.. Particles vibrate more rapidly and their average spacing usually increases on heating. The particles themselves do not expand.

questions.prompt:
Four different substances were transferred from a test tube to a beaker.  The table below shows changes of shape or volume which occurred.
  Substance | Did it change its shape when transferred? | Did it change its volume when transferred?
A | YES | YES
B | YES | NO
C | NO | YES
D | NO | NO
Which substance was solid?
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — D. D. D keeps both its shape and volume, as expected for a solid.
